title: MacroGuide: Topological Guidance for Macrocycle Generation
claim: Periodic corrective guidance steps push a sampling trajectory out of the default failure region into the desired target region.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right, two trajectories over stacked colored regions, legend below
description: A single wide schematic shows two zigzag sampling trajectories that start from one black dot labeled Noise x_T at the left. The background is split into a light green upper band (Cyclic structures) and a light blue-lavender lower band (Non-cyclic structures). The lower blue path uses only denoising steps. It ends in a grey blob labeled Original x_0 (p_original). The upper path alternates blue denoising steps with red arrows for topological guidance steps that lift it into the green region. It ends at a red dot labeled Guided x_0, inside a green density blob (p_MacroGuide). A dashed rounded box on the right is labeled Valid molecules, with Macrocycles in green at its top. A legend at the bottom names the blue arrows as denoising steps and the red arrows as topological guidance steps. The eye goes first to the colored arrows and the two contrasting blobs.
caption: Method overview. \name drives the denoising trajectory towards macrocyclic structures using updates from a topological objective.
abstract: Macrocycles are ring-shaped molecules that offer a promising alternative to small-molecule drugs due to their enhanced selectivity and binding affinity against difficult targets. Despite their chemical value, they remain underexplored in generative modeling, likely owing to their scarcity in public datasets and the challenges of enforcing topological constraints in standard deep generative models. We introduce MacroGuide: Topological Guidance for Macrocycle Generation, a diffusion guidance mechanism that uses Persistent Homology to steer the sampling of pretrained molecular generative models toward the generation of macrocycles, in both unconditional and conditional (protein pocket) settings. At each denoising step, MacroGuide constructs a Vietoris-Rips complex from atomic positions and promotes ring formation by optimizing persistent homology features. Empirically, applying MacroGuide to pretrained diffusion models increases macrocycle generation rates from 1% to 99%, while matching or exceeding state-of-the-art performance on key quality metrics such as chemical validity, diversity, and PoseBusters checks.
